Prepares the runtime container from the environment the runtime chart injects and
then runs as its init: it reaps orphaned processes, forwards termination signals to
what it started, and exits with the code of the work it was running.

Every mode writes the kubeconfig for the pod's service account, restores private modes
under ~/.ssh, creates the outputs directory, adds the provisioned registry credential
to ~/.docker/config.json where it has none, starts sshd and its activity proxy when
ERUN_SSHD_ENABLED is set, and starts the activity monitor (which stops a cloud host
once its idle policy fires).

devops (the default) then bounds the go build cache, clones mounted source or links
the baked release tree, writes the erun config and the platform alias, configures
Codex and Claude Code (instructions, skills, agents, settings, MCP server), installs
the shell hook, serves the MCP edge, and keeps running until the container is stopped.
Any other COMMAND runs after the common preparation, and the container exits with its
code. Runs only on Linux, as the container's init; --dry-run lists what this container
would do without changing anything.

Usage:
  erun runtime-init [devops | COMMAND [ARGS...]] [flags]

Examples:
  erun runtime-init --dry-run
  erun runtime-init devops
  erun runtime-init -- bash -lc 'erun doctor'

Flags:
      --dry-run   Resolve and trace mutating actions without executing them.
  -h, --help      help for runtime-init

Global Flags:
      --output string   Result format: text (default, human stream) or json (structured result on stdout for orchestrators). (default "text")
      --time            Print the elapsed runtime after the command finishes.
  -v, --verbose count   Increase verbosity: -v streams external tool output, -vv adds erun command traces.
